headline: Committee reviews disaster recovery funds and proposed grant rules

meeting.body: Maui County Council Budget, Finance, and Economic Development Committee
meeting.voteItem: Designate BDO Government Services as a resource under Rule 18A
meeting.summary: The committee heard a $1.6 billion disaster recovery funding update and a first look at proposed county grant rules, deferring both items.
meeting.recap: The update covered $1.6 billion in disaster recovery funds from HUD.[[0:21:56]] Staff said $1.39 billion has been obligated, meaning set aside for specific programs.[[0:24:00]] Staff said about 1,100 households are in interim housing.[[0:37:12]] Staff said 83 shopping letters have been issued in the first-time homebuyer program.[[1:01:28]] Staff said 577 housing units are completed, 400 are under construction and 597 are in progress.[[1:21:36]] The chair deferred the disaster recovery item.[[1:38:37]] The second item was a first look at proposed countywide rules for managing county grants.[[1:39:43]] The budget director said the rules cover fiscal sponsors, insurance, record keeping, paying out funds and monitoring.[[1:44:29]] A public meeting on the rules is set for October 7 at the Wailuku Community Center.[[1:56:02]] The administration said the rules will not apply to agreements already in place.[[2:00:00]] Council members' comments on the rules are due by 5 p.m. on August 25.[[2:30:47]] The chair deferred the grants item and adjourned the meeting.[[2:31:50]]
decided: Members had no objection to naming BDO Government Services as a resource for the meeting.
The chair deferred the grants rules item with no vote.
meeting.next: The administration said it will check with the Department of Transportation about one section of the rules.

boards.name: Budget, Finance, and Economic Development Committee

issues.oneLine: The county is working to move households from temporary housing into permanent homes.
issues.why: A council member asked what will happen to people in temporary housing when FEMA leaves before permanent housing is finished.
issues.next: Staff said the county will take over one of the interim housing sites.
issues.brief: Staff said about 1,100 households are in interim housing.[[#1]] Staff said 83 shopping letters have been issued in the first-time homebuyer program.[[#2]] Staff said 577 housing units are completed, 400 are under construction and 597 are in progress.[[#3]] Staff said the funding for multifamily rebuilds requires them to give fire survivors priority to move back.[[#4]]

issues.oneLine: The county is spending $1.6 billion in disaster recovery block grant funds from HUD.
issues.why: Staff said the funds are geared primarily toward helping housing.

deadlines.t: June 30 quarterly report to the council.
HUD grantee gathering hosted on Maui.

issues.brief: Staff said $1.39 billion of the $1.6 billion has been obligated, meaning set aside for programs.[[#1]] Staff said the county deals directly with the federal government on these funds, with no state in the middle.[[#2]] Staff said it is a six-year grant with spending projected through 2031.[[#3]] Staff named rising infrastructure costs as a key risk.[[#4]]
